title: Nagrand
body: Nagrand is one of the few green lands left on shattered Draenor, rolling grasslands that survived largely untouched while great islands of earth drift above the plains. For the orcs, Oshu'gun, the diamond mountain in the southwest, was the heart of their faith: the clans gathered beneath it each spring, and their shaman spoke there with the ancestors. Now the Mag'har hold Garadar in the north, the Kurenai Broken have reclaimed Telaar in the south, ogre clans fight over the hills and the Earthen Ring struggles to calm the restless elements.

title: Garadar
body: Garadar, home of the Mag'har, stands in northern Nagrand. Its people call themselves survivors of the red pox and of a shattered world, and because they were kept apart from the rest of their race, they never shared the corruption that turned other orcs green. The town is under strain: refugees and orphans crowd its streets, the Greatmother who raised nearly every orc here lies ill in her hospice, and the young war chief Garrosh broods by the fire.

parts.body: Greatmother Geyah is the mother of Durotan, who left Draenor long ago with his mate Draka, and when word came that Durotan's son lives and leads the Horde, she wept and begged to see her grandchild.

parts.body: Her grandson came, bearing the Doomhammer, and Geyah knew him at once. She gave Thrall the name Durotan had chosen for his unborn son: Go'el.

title: Telaar
body: In the far south of Nagrand lies Telaar, one of the very few draenei towns on Draenor whose graceful architecture survived intact. It is home now to the Kurenai, a tribe of Broken who escaped their slavers and work to overcome their demonic taint; their name means redeemed. They took the town back only recently under Arechron, welcome the Alliance their draenei kin have joined, and never forget the old hatred between the Broken and the orcs.

parts.body: The Murkblood Broken who sacked the Mag'har village of Sunspring answer to the bog lord Musel'ek of Coilfang, and their leader was once Arechron's friend, a noble Broken wise in the ways of the elements.

title: Halaa
body: On a plateau in the heart of Nagrand stand the empty halls of Halaa, once the foremost draenei research site for the study of naaru crystals. Its builders are long gone, but their notes on the crystals of Oshu'gun remain, and powder from the diamond mountain lies in the earth all around. That prize has drawn the Alliance and the Horde into open war, and rarely does a banner fly over Halaa for long.

title: The Throne of the Elements
body: In the northern hills beyond Skysong Lake rises the Throne of the Elements, where the spirits of Nagrand are honored and the four furies dwell in person: Gordawg of earth, Incineratus of fire, Aborius of water and Kalandrios of air. Shaman of the Earthen Ring keep the site, some of them Broken, and they fear for a world whose people fight on while the elements themselves are in turmoil.

parts.body: Among those who foul Nagrand's waters are the Lost Ones of Windyreed Village, dredging the lakes into marsh, and the Broken elementalists of the Throne admit with shame that they are their own kin.

title: Oshu'gun
body: Oshu'gun, the diamond mountain, towers over southwestern Nagrand, a vast crystal glittering above the plains. Every spring the orc clans gathered here and their shaman communed with the ancestors in its shadow, until the clans became a horde and the spirits fell silent. Now orc ancestors drift across the Spirit Fields toward it as if called, the Consortium covets its crystals, and Shadow Council ritualists have crept inside.

parts.body: The mountain is no stone: it is the wreck of the vessel that first carried the draenei across the stars, and in it lingers the naaru K'ure, whose weakened Light has never escaped.
sources: quest 10101 description (diamond mountain, springtime festival, shaman communed, clans became a horde, spirits silent)

parts.body: As K'ure's Light bled away a void grew in its place, devouring the souls of generations of orcs, and the Burning Legion has learned to harness it.

title: Burning Blade Ruins
body: East of Telaar the Burning Blade Ruins hold the largest gathering of Boulderfist ogres in southern Nagrand, great pyres burning on the upper levels. From here the ogres have struck at their neighbors, driving the Bleeding Hollow from their village, and the Kurenai fear that the ogre hunting parties ranging toward Telaar are the forerunners of an invasion.

parts.body: The Boulderfist did not come by choice: a new clan, the Warmaul, has taken their lands in the north and drives them ever further south.
sources: quest 9921 description (largest collection of Boulderfist, east of Telaar near Terokkar)

parts.body: The Boulderfist answer to an orc: an aged blademaster who went through the Dark Portal a generation ago and has come home, keeping to an upper platform of these very ruins.

title: Forge Camps Hate and Fear
body: In the far west of Nagrand the Burning Legion has raised two forge camps, Hate and Fear, each with a forge, warding towers and a transporter linking it to the Legion's armies, and each ruled by a pit lord overseer. Watching them from a camp of his own is Altruis the Sufferer, a night elf demon hunter who came to Outland in Illidan's service and left it, believing his old master has become the very thing he swore to fight.

parts.body: The camps were designed by a mo'arg engineer who now drinks in the Lower City of Shattrath, and their own fel cannons, turned around, halted the Legion's advance in western Nagrand.
